# SPD-032 — Bash hook allows any script named spud, skipping the permission prompt

## Brief
bash_reason returns permissionDecision allow for a well-formed spud call, and a call is recognized by the script's name: python3.14 /tmp/any/spud board is allowed although /tmp/any/spud is not the ledger's launcher. Whoever can write a file named spud (or a spud_ledger.py beside a link to the launcher) runs it with no permission prompt. SPD-029 widened recognition to case folds and symlinks, which Law 6's refusals need; the allow should need more than recognition.

Evidence: Scratch SPUD_HOME, member: 'python3.14 /tmp/any/spud board' -> allow, reason 'a well-formed spud call by SPUD-001/..., checked by the ledger hook' (before and after SPD-029). Fix sketch: keep recognizing by name for the refusals, but allow only when the script is, by file identity, the ledger root's or a listed worktree's bin/spud; otherwise stay silent and let the harness prompt.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus (the persona's tier), no children: the allow decision for spud calls in bash_reason and launcher identity, with red-first tests, on the SPD-030 shell model now on main. No Fable today (Eric's budget). Code ticket: worktree spd-032-spud-allow-identity. SPD-034 follows in its own worktree after this one returns, since both change bash_reason.
